reasons: Lake record is verified and identifies the case as Gooding v. United States, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1974-04-29.
Lake citations list official citation 416 U.S. 430, parallel citations 94 S. Ct. 1780 and 40 L. Ed. 2d 250, and vendor citation 1974 U.S. LEXIS 133.
The opinion frames the case as a challenge to evidence seized at nighttime under a search warrant executed at about 9:30 p.m.
The Court resolved which statute governed nighttime execution and what showing was required, so the home role Related (nighttime execution) is supported.
The opinion concludes that 21 U.S.C. § 879(a) requires no special showing for a nighttime search beyond showing that contraband is likely to be on the property or person searched at that time.
The opinion also states that the affidavit's showing of continuing drug traffic and a prior informer purchase was sufficient to satisfy § 879(a).
reviewed.suggested_tightening: For maximum fidelity to the opinion, consider replacing premises with property or person to be searched.
